solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Townsman’s work yours truly had installed in vessel (7)

indicatorNotes.installed in: ID is fitted inside the vessel PAN

blocks.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
I'd = I had, the setter speaking as 'yours truly'

annotation.surface: A townsman's handiwork, which the writer has carefully fitted inside some vessel.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': Townsman is OP followed by P(ID)AN. OPPIDAN is the word for a town-dweller, also used at Eton for a pupil who is not a scholar.
annotation.definitionFit: Oppidan comes from Latin oppidum, a town, so an oppidan is a townsman.

entries.clue: Old church group spotted cat (6)

blocks.note: a lot = a group, a batch

annotation.surface: An old church congregation notices a cat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like a verb, as if a church group saw a cat; it belongs to the definition as an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild American cat with a spotted, blotched coat.

entries.clue: Commotion over bishop’s food flavourer (7)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, 'over' puts POTHER above B

blocks.note: a pother is a fuss or commotion
B = bishop, as in chess notation

annotation.surface: A fuss breaks out over the bishop's seasoning.
annotation.walkthrough: The break is POT-HERB, not POTHER-B in meaning: a pot-herb is any herb grown to flavour cooking.
annotation.definitionFit: A potherb is a plant grown to flavour or be cooked in food.

entries.clue: Prepare small tin for nun, perhaps (9)

blocks.note: to do a dish = to prepare it

annotation.surface: Someone is told to get a little tin ready for a nun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks nun as one example: Dominicans are also friars.
annotation.definitionFit: The Dominican order, founded by St Dominic, includes nuns as well as friars.

entries.clue: Retreats shortly to be set up — about a thousand (5)

indicatorNotes.to be set up: in a down clue, set up = raised, so SOON is read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.about: the reversed word goes about, around, the K

annotation.surface: Someone will soon be setting up some quiet refuges, around a thousand of them.
annotation.walkthrough: NOOS goes round K: NOO(K)S. 'About a thousand' reads as an estimate but splits into a container indicator and K.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: nooks are secluded corners, places to retreat to.

entries.clue: Notes as poetry, for the most part (7)

indicatorNotes.for the most part: most of VERSE, losing its last letter

blocks.note: qua = as, in the capacity of

annotation.surface: Someone's jottings read like poetry, mostly.
annotation.walkthrough: QUA, Latin for 'as', is a crossword staple, as in 'qua artist'.
annotation.definitionFit: A quaver is a musical note, an eighth note; quavers are notes.

entries.clue: Amount worker possibly charges to leave before third of May (8)

indicatorNotes.possibly: an ant is one example of a worker
indicatorNotes.charges: the ANT charges into QUIT, landing inside it
indicatorNotes.before: 'before' says the first chunk is written ahead of the Y, reading left to right
indicatorNotes.third of: take the third letter of May

annotation.surface: A worker has a sum levied on leaving before the start of May.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like fees, the likeliest route to an amount; here it is the ant rushing into QUIT.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a quantity is an amount of something.

entries.clue: A shot framing unknown speaker of Indic language once (5)

indicatorNotes.framing: RAN goes round Y like a frame

blocks.note: shot = ran, as in 'shot out of the room'
x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns

annotation.surface: A photograph frames some mysterious person who spoke an old Indian tongue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests a photo or gunfire; it is the past tense of dashing off. 'Aryan' in its old sense named the early Indo-Iranian peoples and their speech.
annotation.definitionFit: The Aryans were the ancient people whose language was the ancestor of the Indic tongues.

entries.clue: One who puts up English official in Scottish university (7)

blocks.note: Scottish universities elect a rector, often a celebrity

annotation.surface: An Englishman has been elected to a post at a Scottish university.
annotation.walkthrough: The Scottish detail matters: at the ancient Scottish universities the rector is an official elected by the students.
annotation.definitionFit: To erect is to put up, so an erector is one who puts things up.

entries.clue: Circus performer, one broadcasting about information’s barrier (5-9)

indicatorNotes.about: SOWER goes about, around, WORD'S WALL

blocks.note: a sower broadcasts seed by scattering it

annotation.surface: A circus act is compared to a radio announcer talking about some obstacle to news.
annotation.walkthrough: S(WORDSWALL)OWER. 'Broadcasting' suggests radio, but to broadcast seed is to scatter it by hand, which is what a sower does.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by type: swallowing swords is a traditional circus and sideshow act.

entries.clue: Captivate in eleventh rally (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits in the next words

blocks.note: the run starts at the second E of eleventh and stops three letters into rally

annotation.surface: A tennis rally in the eleventh game holds the crowd spellbound.
annotation.walkthrough: The seven letters run across the join of the two words, ignoring the space.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to enthral someone is to hold them spellbound.

entries.clue: Spitz-type dogs the Spanish king harasses (9)

annotation.surface: Some dogs pester the King of Spain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The Spanish king' looks like one person; it splits into EL and K.
annotation.definitionFit: The Norwegian elkhound is a spitz breed, bred to hunt elk.

entries.clue: Swallowed by pet, a luscious bone (5)

indicatorNotes.Swallowed by: the answer is inside the next words

blocks.note: the last letter of pet, the word a, and the first three letters of luscious

annotation.surface: A pet wolfs down a juicy bone.
annotation.walkthrough: The dog-and-bone scene hides the fact that the bone named is anatomical.
annotation.definitionFit: Specific for general: the talus is the ankle bone that the tibia rests on.

entries.clue: Boxer divides shares into a revised logical reasoning (15)

indicatorNotes.divides: ALI splits RATIONS, landing inside it
indicatorNotes.revised: INTO A is rewritten as ATION

blocks.note: Muhammad Ali, the crossword's standard boxer

annotation.surface: A boxer splits his earnings into a new round of reasoning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like the word that places the boxer; it is anagram fodder, and 'divides' does the placing. Rationalisation often means inventing reasons after the fact, but here it is logical reasoning.
annotation.definitionFit: Rationalisation is the act of reasoning something through logically.

entries.clue: Oil producer left at home with children (7)

blocks.note: seed = offspring, children, as in the Bible

annotation.surface: An oil tycoon has been left at home minding the kids.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oil producer' suggests a company or state; it is the seed pressed for linseed oil.
annotation.definitionFit: Linseed, the seed of flax, is pressed to produce linseed oil.

entries.clue: Former partner, short-term, not prepared in advance (11)

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner

annotation.surface: A former partner was only ever a short-term, unplanned fling.
annotation.definitionFit: Extemporary means done on the spur of the moment, without preparation.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma splits the clue into three parts, and the last, 'not prepared in advance', is the definition.

entries.clue: Desperately look and see next protective covering (11)

indicatorNotes.Desperately: the letters of LOOK SEE NEXT are thrown about in desperation

annotation.surface: Someone searches frantically for somewhere safe to shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder skips the 'and' between look and see.
annotation.definitionFit: An exoskeleton is the hard outer shell protecting insects and crustaceans.

entries.clue: Round container crossing end of huge expanse of water (5)

indicatorNotes.crossing: CAN goes across, round, the E
indicatorNotes.end of: take the last letter of huge

annotation.surface: A round tub is carried across the end of some enormous body of water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Huge expanse' reads as one phrase; only its E is wordplay and the definition is 'expanse of water'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an ocean is one of the great bodies of salt water.

entries.clue: Light material from French composer including new tango (7)

blocks.note: Erik Satie, composer of the Gymnopédies
T is Tango in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A light fabric comes from a French composer whose new work includes a tango.
annotation.walkthrough: SATI(N)E, then T. 'Tango' suggests music to go with the composer; it is only the letter T.
annotation.definitionFit: Satinet is a thin, light satin or satin-like fabric.

entries.clue: What a careless roadmender does for a quick bite? (4,5)

annotation.definition: What a careless roadmender does for a quick bite?
annotation.surface: A riddle about a clumsy road worker who is really after a snack.
annotation.walkthrough: Read DROP SCONE as 'drops cone': the careless roadmender lets a traffic cone fall. A drop scone is a small thick pancake.
annotation.definitionFit: A drop scone, or Scotch pancake, is a small quick snack cooked on a griddle.

blocks.note: the surface reading: a workman lets one of his traffic cones fall
the setter's reading: a small snack, a pancake made on a griddle

entries.clue: Wrong way for architect to stand — we’ll have to start again (4,2,3,7,5)

annotation.definition2: Wrong way for architect to stand

blocks.clueFragment: Wrong way for architect to stand
blocks.note: read literally: an architect standing facing away from where the plans are drawn
the idiom for abandoning a plan and starting over

annotation.surface: An architect has got his posture wrong, and the whole project must start over.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half takes the idiom literally: someone standing with their back to their drawing board faces the wrong way.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Back to the drawing board' is what you say when a plan fails and you must begin again.

entries.clue: Obstruction after outing, one of several (7)

indicatorNotes.after: 'after' says the obstruction comes after the outing, so it is written second

blocks.note: let = hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

annotation.surface: A roadblock after a day out stops one of a group.
annotation.walkthrough: LET is an old word for obstruction, surviving in 'without let or hindrance' and in tennis, where a let is a net interference.
annotation.definitionFit: A triplet is one of three born together, so one of several.

entries.clue: Just — and even-tempered about it (9)

annotation.surface: A description of a fair-minded person who stays calm about it all.
annotation.walkthrough: EQU(IT)ABLE. 'Just' looks like a throwaway adverb, set off by the dash; it is the adjective meaning fair.
annotation.definitionFit: Equitable means fair and impartial, which is just.

entries.clue: Good Parisian article covering journal in Italian city (7)

blocks.note: a log is a journal, as a ship's log

annotation.surface: A French paper's good article covers a diary kept in an Italian city.
annotation.walkthrough: BO(LOG)N + A. 'Parisian article' wants to be LE or LA; the French goes with 'good' and the article is English A.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Bologna is the capital of Emilia-Romagna, in northern Italy.

entries.clue: Literary work dealing with idle ne’er-do-well (8)

blocks.note: a lay is a narrative poem or song
about = dealing with, on the subject of

annotation.surface: A book whose subject is a lazy good-for-nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dealing with' reads as one phrase; 'dealing' alone gives ABOUT and 'with' links to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A layabout is an idle, work-shy person.

entries.clue: In Provencal city very quietly finish part of book (8)

indicatorNotes.In: 'In' is the city holding the rest, so PP and END are placed inside AIX

blocks.note: pp = pianissimo, very quietly in music

annotation.surface: Someone in a city in Provence quietly finishes part of a book.
annotation.walkthrough: A(PP END)IX. 'Very quietly' is a musical direction.
annotation.definitionFit: An appendix is a section of extra material at the end of a book.

entries.clue: Branch of religion Britney Spears, Mike and I abandoned (15)

indicatorNotes.abandoned: the letters are let loose, wildly rearranged

blocks.note: M is Mike in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A pop singer and two companions are said to have left a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as leaving the faith, the natural surface; it means wild, uninhibited, and tells you to jumble.
annotation.definitionFit: Presbyterianism is the branch of Protestant Christianity governed by elders.

entries.clue: Old measure identified by US president and English Liberal (6)

annotation.surface: An old policy is pinned on an American president and an English Liberal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Measure' suggests a political measure, a policy, in this company of politicians.
annotation.definitionFit: The bushel is an old unit of dry volume, eight gallons.

entries.clue: Nerve-wracking occupation for farm worker (9)

blocks.note: dragging a spiked frame over ploughed soil to break it up

annotation.surface: Farm work described as a stressful job.
annotation.walkthrough: The figurative sense comes from the literal: a harrow drags spikes through the soil.
annotation.definitionFit: Harrowing means acutely distressing, and harrowing is also the farm task of drawing a harrow.

entries.clue: Burlesque involving large heraldic device (7)

blocks.note: a burlesque is a mocking send-up, a satire
L = large, as on clothing sizes

annotation.surface: A spoof that features a large coat of arms.
annotation.walkthrough: SA(L)TIRE. A saltire is the diagonal St Andrew's cross on Scotland's flag.
annotation.definitionFit: A saltire is a heraldic charge in the form of a diagonal cross.

entries.clue: Used to be upset greeting the French, a short time ago but no longer (8)

annotation.definition: a short time ago but no longer

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset = turned upside down, so WERE reads bottom to top

blocks.note: were = used to be, the past of are

annotation.surface: Someone was annoyed by a French hello not long ago, but no more.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Used to be upset' reads as a state of mind; 'used to be' is WERE and 'upset' flips it.
annotation.definitionFit: Erewhile is an archaic word for a little while ago, formerly.

entries.clue: Work from Verdi’s time sent for revision (14)

indicatorNotes.for revision: the letters are revised, reworked into a new order

annotation.surface: A score from Verdi's day is sent off to be revised.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in Verdi's is ignored, as crosswords allow. A divertissement is a light entertainment, a ballet interlude or short piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A divertissement is a musical or balletic work, a light entertainment.

entries.clue: Bond, for example, a man of refinement (5)

annotation.surface: James Bond described as a man of refinement.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a straight description of Bond, which is why the split A + GENT is easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: James Bond, 007, is the best-known fictional secret agent.

entries.clue: Great success, one secured by President Hoover originally (7)

indicatorNotes.secured by: to be secured by something is to be held fast in it, so TRUMP holds I
indicatorNotes.originally: take the first letter of Hoover

annotation.surface: President Hoover is credited with a great success.
annotation.walkthrough: 'President Hoover' is one man on the surface; the president is TRUMP and Hoover only gives H.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a triumph is a great victory or achievement.

entries.clue: Salmon spear odd members of crew removed from Midlands city (7)

indicatorNotes.odd members of: take the 1st and 3rd letters of crew
indicatorNotes.removed from: those letters are taken out of the city

blocks.note: C-r-E-w: odd letters C and E, removed

annotation.surface: A fishing spear is taken from Leicester along with some of the boat's crew.
annotation.walkthrough: LEI(CE)STER loses CE. A leister is a pronged spear for catching salmon.
annotation.definitionFit: A leister is a three-pronged fish spear, used for salmon.

entries.clue: Ring grazing land to get to grips with key publicity for drink (9)

blocks.note: a range is open grazing land
surface padding: it only sets the second pair beside the first

annotation.surface: A plan to fence grazing land and get a grip on key advertising for a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To get to grips with' only brings the two halves together: ORANGE grapples with ADE. Note AD comes before the key E in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Orangeade is an orange-flavoured soft drink.

entries.clue: It supports logs as well as metal (7)

annotation.surface: A metal stand that holds up firewood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As well as' looks like part of a sentence about the thing's uses; it gives AND.
annotation.definitionFit: An andiron is a metal bracket in a fireplace that holds up burning logs.

entries.clue: Dungeon somehow built to encourage remorse ultimately (9)

indicatorNotes.somehow: BUILT TO is arranged in some other way
indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the last letters of encourage and remorse

annotation.surface: A dungeon designed specifically to make its prisoners repent.
annotation.walkthrough: An oubliette is a dungeon reached only by a trapdoor, from French oublier, to forget.
annotation.definitionFit: An oubliette is a secret dungeon with an opening only at the top.

entries.clue: What helps those on the shelf keep upright? (7)

annotation.definition: What helps those on the shelf keep upright?
annotation.surface: A question about propping up people who were left 'on the shelf', unmarried.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Those on the shelf' suggests people passed over for marriage; they are books, and a bookend holds them up.
annotation.definitionFit: A bookend is a support placed at the end of a row of books to keep them upright.

blocks.clueFragment: What helps those on the shelf
blocks.note: the surface reading: 'on the shelf' is an old phrase for people passed over for marriage
the setter's reading: the shelf is literal, and those on it are books being held up

entries.clue: A contemptuous exclamation, stupid! (5)

annotation.surface: Someone scoffs at another, calling them stupid.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word, which the surface makes into the insult being exclaimed.
annotation.definitionFit: Apish means ape-like, and so silly or foolish.

entries.clue: Like symbol, something carried by a lot of rodents (7)

indicatorNotes.a lot of: most of MICE, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: a tote is a bag you carry, a tote bag

annotation.surface: Something ceremonial is lugged about by a crowd of rats and mice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A lot of rodents' reads as a big number of them; it means most of the word MICE.
annotation.definitionFit: Totemic means relating to or acting as a totem, an emblem or symbol.

entries.clue: Doctor enticed extremely pliable creepy-crawly (9)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered
indicatorNotes.extremely: take the outer letters of pliable

annotation.surface: A physician lured some very bendy bug.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person at the start of a sentence; it is the verb, to tamper with.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: creepy-crawly is the informal word for any small crawling creature, and the centipede is one.

entries.clue: Specific sibling’s dissertation? (6)

blocks.note: the is the definite article, pointing to a specific one
sis = sister, a sibling; the 's joins it to the definition

annotation.surface: A question: is this the dissertation belonging to a particular brother or sister?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Specific' gives THE because the definite article marks a specific thing, as opposed to 'a'.
annotation.definitionFit: A thesis is a dissertation written for a university degree.

entries.clue: Current trap in exam is without precedent (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places I and GIN within the word ORAL, splitting it as OR…AL

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken exam
I is the symbol for electric current
a gin is a snare or trap

annotation.surface: A pitfall in an ongoing exam is unheard of.
annotation.walkthrough: OR(I GIN)AL. 'Current' looks like 'present day'; it is the physics symbol I.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: what is original is new, the first of its kind, so nothing came before it.

entries.clue: Foolish person to pay for weed (9)

blocks.note: a goose is a silly person
to foot the bill = to pay it

annotation.surface: An idiot has to fork out for some cannabis.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Weed' suggests cannabis; it is the plant family that includes fat hen.
annotation.definitionFit: Goosefoot is a common weed, named for its leaf shape.

entries.clue: Fish, cheese and eggs served up (8)

indicatorNotes.served up: in a down clue, 'up' reverses YARG NITS to read bottom to top

blocks.note: Yarg is a Cornish cheese wrapped in nettles
nits are the eggs of lice

annotation.surface: A menu of fish, cheese and eggs is brought to the table.
annotation.walkthrough: YARGNITS reversed. The cheese is the odd one out: Yarg, from Cornwall, is a favourite of setters for exactly this reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: The stingray is a flat fish with a venomous spine in its tail.

entries.clue: I’ve reported delay entering West Sussex town, mature and very helpful (5,4,6,2,4)

indicatorNotes.reported: ONE'S WAIT is heard as ONE'S WEIGHT

blocks.note: Worthing, a seaside town in West Sussex
I've = one has = one's; delay = wait

annotation.surface: Someone complains of a hold-up getting into a Sussex resort.
annotation.walkthrough: WORTH(ONE'S WEIGHT)ING + OLD. 'I've' is 'one has', shortened to one's, the formal third person the setter uses for himself.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone so useful that they would be worth their body's weight in gold.

entries.clue: Driver’s bet inspiring cricket side (7)

indicatorNotes.inspiring: to inspire is to breathe in, so WAGER takes ON inside

blocks.note: the on side, or leg side, of a cricket field

annotation.surface: A racing driver's bet encourages a cricket team.
annotation.walkthrough: WAG(ON)ER. The 's is 'is'. The on side is the half of a cricket field on the batter's legs side.
annotation.definitionFit: A wagoner is the driver of a horse-drawn wagon.

entries.clue: Revelation of trade exhibition’s a laugh at first (7)

indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letter of laugh

blocks.note: an expo is a trade exhibition, with the 's

annotation.surface: A trade fair turns out to be a joke from the start.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At first' could apply to 'a laugh' as a whole; it takes only the L.
annotation.definitionFit: Exposal is a rarer form of exposure, a revealing.

entries.clue: Member of band, perhaps, finally accepted stranger (7)

indicatorNotes.finally: take the last letter of accepted

blocks.note: rum = odd, so rummer = odder, stranger

annotation.surface: A newcomer is at last welcomed into a group, perhaps a rock band.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' reads as a noun, the outsider accepted into the band; it is the comparative adjective, RUMMER.
annotation.definitionFit: A drummer is one member of a band; 'perhaps' because others play different instruments.

entries.clue: Seabird is shade of blue, reportedly (6)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is heard, not what is written

blocks.note: petrol blue is a deep greenish blue

annotation.surface: A seabird is said to be a certain blue colour.
annotation.walkthrough: Petrol blue is a named shade in British fashion and paint, after the sheen of petrol on water.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: petrels, storm petrels included, are oceanic seabirds.

entries.clue: £1,000 rise arranged for old man once (9)

blocks.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds

annotation.surface: A pay rise of a thousand pounds is agreed for an elderly man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old man' here is a grandfather, and 'once' flags that grandsire is archaic.
annotation.definitionFit: Grandsire is an old word for grandfather, an old man in the family.

entries.clue: Flood from river surrounded by hilly ground (5)

indicatorNotes.surrounded by: the river is surrounded by the hills, so R sits inside DOWN

blocks.note: downs are rolling chalk hills, like the South Downs

annotation.surface: A river bursts its banks among the hills.
annotation.walkthrough: D(R)OWN. In Britain a down is open rolling upland, which is why 'down' can mean hilly ground.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the transitive sense: to drown fields means to submerge them.

entries.clue: Atonement of head of zoo leaving Cornish resort (7)

indicatorNotes.head of: take the first letter of zoo
indicatorNotes.leaving: the Z leaves the town's name

annotation.surface: A zookeeper walks out of a Cornish seaside town, making amends for something.
annotation.walkthrough: PEN(Z)ANCE loses its Z. 'Head of zoo' suggests the zoo's director.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a penance is a punishment undertaken to make amends for sin.

entries.clue: Arrest former pupil, man of substance (5)

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil

annotation.surface: Police arrest an old boy of the school, a wealthy man.
annotation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is the British term for a former pupil of a school.
annotation.definitionFit: A nabob is a man of great wealth, originally one who made a fortune in India.

entries.clue: Artist’s supporter heading off sly individual (5)

indicatorNotes.heading off: 'heading off' read as 'head off': the head, the first letter, comes off the word

blocks.note: a weasel is a sly, sneaky person

annotation.surface: A painter's patron sets off, heading away from a crafty type.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a patron or fan; it is the stand that holds the canvas.
annotation.definitionFit: An easel is the frame that supports an artist's canvas.

entries.clue: Study sci-fi film due to be distributed (5)

indicatorNotes.to be distributed: DUE is dealt out in a new order

annotation.surface: A study of a science-fiction film that is about to be released.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Distributed' is film-industry language for release, which is what makes the surface work; here it jumbles DUE.
annotation.definitionFit: An étude is a musical study, a piece written to practise a technique.

entries.clue: Offensive quality no one associated with unspecified head (11)

blocks.note: some = an unspecified one, as in 'some person'
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

annotation.surface: An unpleasant trait that nobody wants linked to their anonymous boss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No one' reads as nobody; split it into NO and I. 'Head' is a headland, which is what ness means in place names.
annotation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, so noisomeness is that offensive quality.

entries.clue: Dramatic performer right to plug Robert’s man excitedly (11)

indicatorNotes.excitedly: the letters are stirred up, jumbled

blocks.note: R = right, added to the fodder
surface padding: it would place R inside, but the whole lot is mixed anyway

annotation.surface: An actor is right to stand up for Robert's servant with great passion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To plug' reads as promoting someone; it only puts R among the letters, and since they are all mixed its position does not matter.
annotation.definitionFit: A barnstormer is a flamboyant actor, originally a strolling player who performed in barns.

entries.clue: Eg novel South African party visiting European capital (7)

annotation.surface: A South African political party makes a trip to a European capital.
annotation.walkthrough: ROM(ANC)E. 'Novel' reads as an adjective, new, but with 'Eg' it is a book, one kind of romance.
annotation.definitionFit: A romance is a kind of novel, a story of love or adventure.

entries.clue: Correspond about nasty smell in chest of drawers (7)

blocks.note: to tally = to correspond, match up

annotation.surface: Letters complain about a foul smell in an old piece of furniture.
annotation.walkthrough: TALL(BO)Y. 'Correspond' suggests writing letters; it means to agree. A tallboy is a tall chest of drawers.
annotation.definitionFit: A tallboy is a tall chest of drawers, often in two sections.

entries.clue: Genuine printing error (7)

blocks.note: actual, true to the words, not exaggerated
printers' jargon for a misprint of a single letter

annotation.walkthrough: The second sense is printers' jargon: a literal is a typo, an error in a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal means true to fact, and in printing a literal is a typographical error.
